brief.name: Dext
brief.summary: Dext is a Visual Studio Code extension for AI conversations and typed workflows, combining Ask, Agent, Plan and Code modes. Its extension host registers commands, sidebar, history, project, API and resource surfaces; routes work to Codex CLI, Claude CLI or DeepSeek Harness; coordinates turns, streaming trace, questions, plans, patch review and persisted history; and executes reusable TypeScript workflows through a long-lived Node kernel. A browser sidebar webview owns the composer, transcript and interaction UI, while a separate project reader webview renders generated knowledge and diagrams. Dext also integrates configured MCP tools over stdio or HTTP and runs its packaged Archify Node runtime for project diagram layout and validation.

evidence.note: Product purpose: AI conversations and typed workflows with agent delegation and implementation plans.
Supported provider integrations: Codex CLI, Claude CLI and DeepSeek Harness.
The sidebar webview build entry is src/webview/main.ts.
The project reader webview build entry is src/features/project/browser/entry.ts.
The Code-mode kernel is built as a separate ESM entry from src/runner/dextKernel.mjs.
MCP dispatch selects the HTTP or stdio transport per configured server.
The Archify runtime resolves from the packaged vendor/project-diagrams directory.
The VS Code extension main entry is dist/extension.js.

capabilities.description: Hosts the conversation sidebar and browser UI, including tab and session navigation, transcript and agent-trace/TODO rendering, output scrolling, interactive questions and forms, plan authoring and continuation, patch review, and persisted History. It coordinates each turn from execution through provider events to rendered results.

capabilities.canonicalName: Agent execution, tools, and provider integration
capabilities.description: Routes runs across Codex, Claude and DeepSeek Harness; spawns CLI calls and maintains Codex app-server conversations; manages DeepSeek Harness ACP sessions, bridge, presets and policy; validates and repairs structured results; resolves agent profiles and model choices; enforces permission and terminal policy; and discovers and invokes MCP tools over stdio or HTTP with scoped credentials.

capabilities.canonicalName: Typed workflow APIs and code-mode runtime
capabilities.description: Defines built-in and custom Dext APIs, generated declarations, API reference signatures and templates; maintains the callable registry and workflow invocation runtime; records conversations into workflow skeletons; discovers Skills; runs workspace TypeScript through a Node code kernel; and resolves workspace context and source-eligibility parsing.

Indexes project sources and builds structure/graph evidence; generates project knowledge, topics, C4 and architecture views and diagrams; serves bounded structure queries through an MCP Node entry; hosts the Project editor, settings, initialization checkpoints and Archify-backed diagram runtime; renders the project reader/viewer; and persists .dext project documents.

capabilities.canonicalName: Composer, context attachments, and editor experience
capabilities.description: Manages unsent conversation drafts and responsive composer overflow; resolves dropped files and reference-aware input insertion; captures selection, file and clipboard attachments into bounded Dext storage; defines reference tokens, chips and decoration; searches files and project objects; provides Monaco editing, Dext TypeScript libraries/auto-import, theme mapping and source highlighting; and renders shared Markdown diagrams, code copy and ready-queued output.

capabilities.canonicalName: Extension shell, shared contracts, and resource surfaces
capabilities.description: Composes extension activation and host services; defines shared Dext contracts and the validated sidebar wire protocol; owns reusable editor-tab lifecycle and the CSP-governed webview document shell; and implements API and Global Resources browser pages with resource contracts, navigation, previews and recoverable missing states.

contexts.purpose: VS Code extension activation and the application-level host composition root. It registers commands, editor tabs, history, project, API and resource surfaces; owns extension lifecycle and disposal; and constructs the services that connect workflow execution, agent profiles and routing, MCP manifests and credentials, resources, plans, storage, workspace settings and shared sidebar state.

contexts.canonicalName: Shared Dext contracts and sidebar wire protocol
contexts.purpose: Shared cross-feature Dext vocabulary and validation, plus the sidebar webview wire protocol. It defines typed invocations, execution metadata, results, UI and MCP interactions, permissions, agent stream events and workflow responses; provides Zod schemas for result, UI, patch, terminal, MCP and kernel payloads; and composes feature-owned conversation schemas and sidebar state into the global request and response unions.

Host-side conversation sidebar. It owns the webview view lifecycle and message bridge for conversations, turns, history and composer input, including attachments, plan and resource actions, file and selection context, deferred messages and webview assets, while delegating execution and conversation state to the conversation services and application host.

Browser-side sidebar composition root. It initializes the VS Code message bridge and shared clients, then wires conversation tabs, composer, transcript, output, plan, patch, agent, resource, search and attachment state into the workspace UI.

contexts.canonicalName: Conversation sessions, history and tab navigation
contexts.purpose: Host and browser conversation lifecycle. It assembles the conversation service stack, hydrates and restores sessions, owns open and active tabs, per-tab agent selection and saved layout, persists pins, favorites, titles and selections, orders history, coalesces agent events, and manages browser tab identity, cached conversation views, tab-strip actions and drag reordering.

contexts.canonicalName: Agent question elicitation and interaction UI
contexts.purpose: Agent input interaction. It maps elicitation JSON-schema forms to shared Dext questions and answers, and renders pending native-agent and structured UI requests as waiting or settled cards with drafts, dialogs, focus and suspension.

contexts.canonicalName: Agent trace, message and TODO presentation
contexts.purpose: Agent output presentation. It normalizes provider TODO updates, filters replayed trace events, parses final-message details, and renders the trace timeline, message content and TODO progress in the conversation webview.

contexts.canonicalName: Agent CLI execution and provider routing
contexts.purpose: Host CLI agent execution. It routes runs across Codex, Claude and DeepSeek Harness backends, spawns one-shot CLI calls and conversations, manages sessions, permissions and structured results, and enforces timeout, tool-activity and terminal-completion signals.

Codex app-server integration. It maintains the JSON-RPC child connection, coordinates conversation turns and input, converts app-server notifications into agent stream events, and extracts Codex error messages.

DeepSeek Harness integration. It discovers installations and presets, resolves launch and sandbox policy, runs ACP turns with session binding, resume and model selection, serves the authenticated private bridge, and converts question and result frames into Dext results.

Structured agent result boundary. It compiles callable definitions into Ax signatures with Zod and JSON Schema validation, recovers and serializes typed results, evaluates workspace-derived assertions, and performs bounded CLI-backed repair of invalid output.

contexts.canonicalName: Built-in workflow APIs and Dext type generation
contexts.purpose: Built-in workflow API surface. It defines agent, planning, template, terminal, skill and UI callables with provider-dependent CLI and model overrides, generates the Dext declaration, compiler project and MCP result types, and supplies composer type notices.

Workspace context capability. It defines the snapshot and reference contract, resolves selection, active-file, explicit file, symbol and directory references for workflows, and captures editor context and opens file references through the VS Code host.

Workflow invocation runtime. It executes typed built-in, agent, MCP, template, UI and conversation or structured-JSON calls, applying workspace policy, result adaptation, diagnostics and repair seams.

Code-mode kernel runtime. It supervises the Node child kernel's startup and handshake, bounded JSON and IPC dispatch, run buffers, exit handling, resume caching and replay logging. The worker imports the user's TypeScript entry, streams console output, settles in-flight Dext calls and reports results, while a warning shim suppresses repeated type-stripping notices.

contexts.canonicalName: Project source indexing and graph analysis
contexts.purpose: Project source indexing and graph analysis. It extracts language, symbol and dependency facts from configured sources with cache reuse and cancellation, and derives ranked file graphs, communities, hubs, cycles and bounded query facts.

contexts.canonicalName: Project AI generation and model quality
contexts.purpose: Project AI generation. It selects and packages indexed evidence, builds and validates prompts and bounded responsibility batches, reconciles and repairs model output, routes requests through the selected agent, resumes long runs from checkpoints, reviews model quality, and defines the persisted knowledge and intent contracts it validates.

Project diagrams and architecture views. It defines diagram, evidence and architecture contracts, owns adapter registration, last-good history and render lifecycle, builds derived structure and class maps, and guards viewer exports, evidence paths and stale work.

Per-conversation unsent drafts and retained draft attachments, responsive composer overflow observation, and the shared webview editor input path: dropped-file resolution through the host, syntax-aware reference insertion, and selection-aware text replacement.

contexts.canonicalName: Context Attachments, Clipboard and Dext Storage
contexts.purpose: Captures editor selections, workspace files, directories and clipboard file paths as Dext references; adds selection hover actions and the webview clipboard bridge; and resolves Dext-owned attachment and plan storage under global or workspace locations with size and count limits, path validation, prompt paths and pruning.

Defines, parses and formats file, symbol, selection, directory, legacy and #name[id] project reference tokens; projects them into removable editor edits, reference chips and display labels; and carries project object identity and display snapshots.
Searches accepted project objects and a cached, fuzzy-ranked workspace file index for picker candidates, using latest-query-wins request/response transports between the webview and host.

End-to-end lifecycle for host-defined questions and UI forms: shared form and answer schemas, pending request brokers with cancellation and focus notifications, browser modal controls with validation, and read-only answer and choice presentation.

Coordinates a conversation turn from a pinned execution snapshot through provider execution, cancellation, buffered events, plan continuation and patch review; defines the host, session, interaction, notifier and patch ports plus the interrupted-run error.

Shared turn presentation model and element builders used by live and History rendering, with the live transcript cache, title handling, and the DOM adapter that binds the shared renderer to the live transcript.

Owns conversation output scrolling and navigation: follow-the-newest versus reader-gesture state, deferred scroll corrections, jump-to-latest and jump-to-top controls, scroll-range diagnostics, and routing external and workspace output links.

Plan-round document protocol and helpers that extract stored Markdown, filter it from streamed output, derive safe filenames and workspace paths, track todo progress, run continuation and verification rounds, settle status, and render Build and Stop controls.

Cross-layer lifecycle for agent-proposed file changes: builds reviewable before and after diffs, owns pending proposals and accept or reject resolution, and applies validated payloads and ranges through VS Code edits and saves.

Persisted conversation, session and turn records plus conversation-scoped library preferences, with bounded serialized memento storage, rename, delete, fork and compatibility normalization, and the History panel's HTML and Markdown rendering, lazy expansion, diffs, terminal output, Plan progress, reference chips and copy actions.

Defines resource authoring and editing contracts for kinds, scopes, naming, documents, sessions, editor data sources, tab and panel options, and API source descriptors; implements the API and Global Resources tabs with stable list and detail pages, navigation, scope switching, searchable trees, source previews, icons and recoverable missing-resource states.

Models and validates the build-generated Node and JavaScript API reference catalog, lazily loads it, extracts documented exported TypeScript functions through Tree-sitter without executing them, and formats callable field types, parameters, result types and conversation-facing method metadata.

Hosts the Project editor tab and composes its overview shell, navigation and embedded settings form; supplies the panel data source and initialization service that assemble persisted overview, knowledge, evidence and diagram data and run cancellable prepare, generate and save initialization with monotonic progress.

Builds and caches the local project structure model, derives candidate responsibility groups and build and runtime boundaries, and packages bounded cited evidence for initialization and diagram generation.

Built as the structureMcp Node entry, this read-only stdio MCP service validates the persisted project structure index, publishes the structure_query tool contract, and executes bounded dependency, consumer, community, hub, search and path queries for agent clients.

Defines the project-diagram adapter boundary and implements Archify: compiles supported diagram kinds into Archify IR, validates and repairs layouts through the external runtime, produces render and export artifacts with validation receipts, and maintains per-diagram snapshots, bounded history, change comparison and JSON-safe history documents.

Derives reader-facing project topics from saved intent and diagram evidence, preserves earlier analyses across model regeneration, checks source freshness and builds C4 context and runtime topics; evaluates declared architecture rules and renders rule, violation and design-decision notes in topic articles and galleries.

Browser-side project reader launched by the project webview build entry: mounts from the host element, renders topic articles and saved diagram galleries, computes playback steps, and embeds a sandboxed Archify viewer with trusted messaging, inspection, playback, fullscreen, export and source navigation.

contexts.canonicalName: Editor Tab Lifecycle and Document Shell
contexts.purpose: Editor-tab infrastructure for Dext panels: stable tab keys and page vocabulary, validated persisted state, one webview panel per key with reuse, adoption, close and restore deduplication, and the shared CSP-governed HTML document shell for project, API, resource and history pages.

Node-side Code-mode execution kernel that maps `dext` and `dext/api/*` imports, loads workspace TypeScript into a fresh per-run module graph, tracks direct workflow calls, dispatches typed API requests over the process channel, enforces the JSON value rule, waits for in-flight calls, and replays recorded calls on retry.

Mutable registry of built-in, global, and project workflow callables. It applies source precedence, tracks a revision, provides stable lookup and sorted listing, and clears externally loaded methods so runtime dispatch and API inspection read one catalog.

Parses Dext template front matter and field declarations, validates placeholders against declared fields, derives provider output schemas and caller presets, renders Markdown, text, JSON, TOML, or YAML, and reports concrete format errors.

Builds an editable TypeScript workflow skeleton from recorded conversation turns, deriving API and file names, shared inputs, confirmation gates, imports, step calls, and result types while preserving unrepresentable Code-mode turns as comments.
Discovers project, configured, and global SKILL.md packages, extracts descriptor metadata, lists skills in stable order, and loads instructions with workspace-containment checks.

Shared workspace-source substrate: parses gitignore-style exclusion rules with negation, anchoring, and directory semantics, and initializes lazily cached Tree-sitter parsers and grammars for structural and API-source analysis.

Shared output path for Markdown and Webview surfaces: buffers host messages until the Webview is ready, renders Mermaid diagrams and copyable fenced code, formats JSON results, and produces elapsed-duration labels.

Monaco-based composer editor that projects source references as atomic private characters, renders reference chips and navigation affordances, and handles reference-aware paste, selection, clipboard, file drops, diagnostics, and run shortcuts.

Stages copied text and file paths behind TTL and byte limits, validates the clipboard state that a paste can consume, and converts resolved text snapshots into content-hashed CodeRefs for attachments and workflow context.

Bootstraps Monaco workers and language contributions, configures the composer's TypeScript compiler, diagnostics, and virtual Dext libraries, and derives importable Dext symbols from declarations and workspace modules for auto-import completion.

Loads the active VS Code TextMate theme, including inherited files and token customizations, into a shared token contract; maps token and editor colors into the Monaco theme; and colorizes conversation source with the same tokenizer and theme.

contexts.canonicalName: Agent Permission Policy and Terminal Execution
contexts.purpose: Defines the shared read-only, workspace-write, and full-access agent permission vocabulary, and executes workflow terminal commands under workspace trust with cwd containment, timeout, output-size, and environment validation.

Owns agent profile, model, preset and permission contracts; TOML-backed Codex configuration and Codex/Claude default and model-cache discovery; resolution of persisted composer selections and effective model options; and presentation of the current selection to the webview.

Owns JSONC MCP manifest parsing, stdio and HTTP server contracts, endpoint and authentication diagnostics, REST tool adapters, transport selection, tool discovery and invocation, and scoped access-token storage.

Owns the project subsystem composition root: wiring project editors, the diagram registry, evidence readers, tab persistence and the initialization checkpoint store; restoring project tabs; and defining validated workspace, tool and evidence-reading defaults and limits.
Owns durable .dext project documents and initialization checkpoints, including schema-tolerant reads, optimistic version checks, atomic checkpoint creation, and VS Code file-system access.

qualityIssues.message: src/features/project/host/persistence/projectInitializationCheckpointStore.ts is grouped under 'Project Persistence', but its only non-type import consumer is src/app/projectSetup.ts in 'Project setup and workspace settings'. Review the responsibility boundary; imports alone do not prove ownership.
qualityIssues.reason: The file declares a VS Code `Uri`-rooted initialization checkpoint-store factory tied to the project-model checkpoint contract. That is durable persistence, matching Project Persistence's explicit atomic-initialization-checkpoint responsibility. `app/projectSetup.ts` is a composition root that wires this store alongside editors, diagrams and other project components, so its sole runtime import does not transfer ownership to setup or workspace settings.

src/platform/browser/markdownDiagrams.ts is grouped under 'Conversation Output Rendering and Delivery', but its only non-type import consumer is src/features/conversations/browser/interactionMarkdown.ts in 'Interactive Questions and Forms'. src/shared/lib/jsonOutput.ts is grouped under 'Conversation Output Rendering and Delivery', but its only non-type import consumer is src/features/conversations/presentation/turnComponents.ts in 'Conversation Transcript and Turn Presentation'. Review the responsibility boundary; imports alone do not prove ownership.

src/features/agents/host/toml.ts is grouped under 'Agent Configuration and MCP Integration', but its only non-type import consumer is src/features/agents/host/agentProfiles.ts in 'Agent profiles and model selection'. Review the responsibility boundary; imports alone do not prove ownership.
qualityIssues.reason: The parser declares only generic TOML helpers such as `parseToml` and `tomlString`, and its only non-type consumer is `agentProfiles.ts`, which owns Codex configuration and model discovery. No MCP member imports it, while `mcpManifest.ts` parses JSONC instead. The import evidence is corroborated by the helper shape and the consumer's profile-configuration responsibility, so ownership moves to Agent profiles and model selection rather than MCP integration.

qualityIssues.message: Files that import each other form one graph community, but they are split across 53 responsibility modules (largest: 'Interactive Questions and Forms'). Compare the module boundaries with these tightly coupled files; the graph is a navigation signal, not proof that the split is wrong.

'Workflow Execution Kernel' spans 2 import communities, and its largest cohesive group is 2/5 files. Check whether distinct features were merged into one module; this is a review signal, not an ownership error.
